extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers and editors submitting to or handling manuscripts for BMC journals
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and ethical policies and practical requirements for preparing, submitting, reviewing and publishing manuscripts in BMC journals, covering ethics, data and materials availability, reporting standards, peer review, misconduct and post-publication actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission implies author agreement with policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript to a BMC journal implies that all authors have read and agreed to its content and that the manuscript conforms to the journal’s policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature remains neutral regarding jurisdictional claims in maps and affiliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate with Respect
rubrics_metrics.description: All staff, authors, reviewers and members of the public must behave professionally and respectfully; no aggressive behaviour, harassment, bullying or discrimination is tolerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious or repeated violations may be reported to employers or authorities; Springer Nature may refuse to interact or do business with offenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics approval for human research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research involving human participants, human material, or human data must have been performed in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and approved by an appropriate ethics committee; manuscripts must include a statement naming the ethics committee and reference number where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If granted an exemption, detail it and the granting committee. Editors may request further documentation or contact the ethics committee; manuscripts may be rejected if research not within appropriate ethical framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective ethics approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If a study did not receive ethics committee approval prior to commencing, retrospective ethics approval usually cannot be obtained and the manuscript may not be considered for peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision to proceed is at the Editor's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: New clinical tools and procedures justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors reporting novel procedures or tools in clinical settings must justify why the new procedure/tool was deemed more appropriate than usual practice to meet the patient's clinical need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the procedure is already approved for clinical use at the authors’ institution, this justification is not required. Ethics approval and informed patient consent expected for experimental use when clear clinical advantage was not apparent prior to treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: Informed consent to participate must be obtained from participants (or parent/legal guardian for children under 16) and a statement must appear in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies involving vulnerable groups may be considered at Editor's discretion and may be referred for further scrutiny. Consent must be obtained for all forms of personally identifiable data; documentary evidence may be requested. For transplantation studies, declare organs/tissues not obtained from prisoners and name institutions providing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving human embryos, gametes and stem cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must confirm experiments complied with relevant guidelines/regulations and include an ethics statement naming the approving committee and describing details; state informed consent and conditions of donation where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of approvals and redacted consent documents may be requested. Authors encouraged to follow 2016 ISSCR Guidelines. Editors consider safety, regulatory compliance and societal debate for germline modification papers; may consult Research Integrity Group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex and gender reporting (SAGER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should follow SAGER guidelines: use sex and gender terms carefully, indicate applicable sex(es) in title/abstract, describe expectation of sex/gender differences, report how these were accounted for, provide disaggregated data where appropriate, and discuss results; if analysis not done, give rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: sex = biological differences; gender = socially constructed roles. Guidelines apply to studies involving humans, vertebrate animals and cell lines. Authors are suggested to consult the full SAGER guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal research ethics and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental research on vertebrates or regulated invertebrates must comply with institutional, national or international guidelines and, where available, be approved by an appropriate ethics committee; manuscripts must include a compliance/approval statement naming the committee and reference number where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions must be detailed with reasons. Editors may reject manuscripts that involve protocols inconsistent with accepted norms; they may contact ethics committees if needed. Do not consider manuscripts using anesthesia/euthanasia methods inconsistent with veterinary best practice (e.g., chloral hydrate, ether, chloroform). For client-owned animals, document informed owner consent and high standard of veterinary care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field studies and non-experimental animal research
rubrics_metrics.description: Field and non-experimental animal studies must comply with relevant guidelines and, where available, have appropriate approvals/permissions and include a statement detailing compliance and permissions/licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors recommended to follow IUCN Policy Statement on Research Involving Species at Risk of Extinction and CITES where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant research permissions and voucher specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental and field plant research must comply with relevant legislation and include a statement specifying permissions/licenses for collection of plant or seed specimens; voucher specimens for wild plants must be deposited in a public herbarium with identification information included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend compliance with IUCN and CITES; deposit voucher specimens to support reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palaeontological and geological sample provenance and deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear provenance for palaeontological specimens and geological samples; submissions should include permissions obtained and issuing authority; type and cited specimens should be deposited in recognised museums with catalogue numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If precise provenance unavailable for older collections, state this; where locality disclosure would compromise site security, exclude detailed locality info. Encourage deposition of 3-D scans in accessible repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with UNESCO and IUCN instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted content must adhere to UNESCO normative instruments for cultural heritage protection and IUCN resolutions and guidance where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to submissions involving heritage or conservation-sensitive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts providing information that could be misapplied to pose significant threats must be evaluated so benefits outweigh risks; editors may require specialized peer review for dual use risk and may decline publication if misuse risk outweighs benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors expected to comply with institutional/funder/national requirements, disclose regulatory status and approvals, and describe containment/biosafety procedures. Editors may take expert advice; published content may be corrected, retracted or removed if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) research
rubrics_metrics.description: CAM research should meet the same evidence threshold as mainstream medicine: comply with international/national standards (e.g., Declaration of Helsinki), be adequately controlled, blinded (where appropriate), randomised and sufficiently powered to interpret effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparing a CAM treatment only to another CAM is insufficient. Supplementing conventional treatment with CAM is valid only if compared to the same conventional treatment with placebo. CAM on animals/humans must have adequate prior objective evidence (e.g., in vitro/cellular work) from peer-reviewed literature; lacking evidence will lead to non-consideration on ethical grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent for publication of identifiable personal details
rubrics_metrics.description: Written informed consent for publication of details, images or videos relating to an individual must be obtained and stated in the manuscript; consent must permit publication under the assigned Creative Commons licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If person deceased, consent from next of kin required. If images are entirely unidentifiable and no personal details reported, consent may not be required; final decision lies with the Editor. Templates for participant publication approval available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective registration of clinical trials in suitable publicly available registries is required for clinical trials reported in manuscripts, in line with ICMJE guidance. The trial registration number (TRN) and registration date should be the last line of the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition of clinical trial per WHO/ICMJE includes phase I–IV; authors unsure whether registration needed should consult ICMJE FAQs. Suitable registries include those on the ICMJE list and WHO ICTRP primary registries (e.g., ISRCTN). Retrospective registration is encouraged if prospectively unregistered; if allowed by the journal, include TRN, date, and 'retrospectively registered' in the abstract last line. Systematic reviews registration (e.g., PROSPERO) is encouraged and registration numbers should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of data and materials — general expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission implies materials and relevant raw data described in the manuscript will be freely available for non-commercial use post-publication without breaching participant confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMC strongly encourages dataset deposition in public repositories or presentation in machine-readable format in manuscripts/additional files. For data types with community norms, deposition may be mandated. Authors needing help can use Author Support portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandated data deposition for certain data types
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain data types (e.g., genomic sequences, nucleic acid/protein sequences), BMC mandates deposition in public repositories upon submission where community standards exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such data must be available to editors and reviewers during peer review and released publicly upon publication. Consult the list of mandated data types and appropriate repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: DNA and RNA sequence deposition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel DNA/RNA sequence and genome assembly data must be deposited in INSDC-participating repositories (or those moving towards inclusion); assembly must be available in addition to raw reads; even short stretches of novel sequence (epitopes, markers) must be deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage supplementing short sequences with surrounding context; sequences of small RNA probes central to conclusions must be provided. Encourage deposition of microbial assemblies from metagenomics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genomics and transcriptomics metadata and annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: When depositing genomic/transcriptomic datasets authors should provide metadata to allow reproduction and include annotations where applicable, especially for unsequenced genomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps reproducibility and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked phenotype-genotype human data access controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Linked phenotype and genotype data for human subjects should be submitted to publicly accessible repositories with appropriate access controls; any restrictions require explanation and details of access conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain nature and reasons for restrictions and conditions of access; maintain participant confidentiality and comply with local data protection laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gene expression (microarray) MIAME compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Data derived from microarray studies must be MIAME-compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure necessary metadata and standards for interpretation and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of clinical datasets — privacy and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must respect participants' privacy and protect identity when publishing clinical datasets; ideally obtain informed consent for dataset publication at recruitment; if not possible, demonstrate that publication does not compromise anonymity or breach local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must state in the submission whether informed consent was obtained; if not, state the reason and which body was consulted. Consider direct/indirect identifiers and consult local ethics committees if anonymity uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software and code availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Any previously unreported software application or custom code should be available for testing by editors and reviewers in a way that preserves reviewer anonymity; manuscripts should include how editors/reviewers can access code and link to archived versions with DOI or unique identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend using Zenodo for GitHub code. If implementation isn't made freely available, manuscript should focus on the underlying method and not discuss the tool in detail. Software should be available for non-commercial use without undue restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use discipline-specific recognized repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, submit data to discipline-specific, community-recognized repositories; where none exist, use a generalist repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See data policy guidance for repository selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of research materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission implies unique materials described (strains, antibodies, cell-lines, mutant lines, etc.) will be freely available to scientists for non-commercial use without breaching confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable payment to cover distribution costs is acceptable; encourage use of established public repositories and listing persistent identifiers/accession numbers. Any restrictions or commercial distribution must be clearly stated in the paper. Suggested statement provided for reagents/tools/materials availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of Data and Materials statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must include an 'Availability of Data and Materials' section detailing where supporting data can be found; if data cannot be shared openly, include a reason and provide it in that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may decline further consideration if restrictions are unduly prohibitive. BMC encourages following ICMJE clinical trial data sharing standards for these statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICMJE-aligned data sharing details for clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: For clinical trial data, statements should specify whether individual de-identified participant data will be shared (undecided not acceptable), what data, related documents, when data will be available and for how long, and by what access criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data dictionaries, protocols, statistical analysis plans where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC endorses FORCE11 Data Citation Principles and requires publicly available datasets to be fully referenced in the reference list with accession number or unique identifier (e.g., DOI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations should include minimum DataCite information and follow journal style; dataset identifiers expressed as full URLs. Example availability statement and reference provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication access to data
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must comply post-publication with the data availability statement and make data available as indicated; inability to produce original data upon request may lead to editorial investigation and potential retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasets expected to be available via community repositories with permanent identifiers where that is the community norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party data and analysis disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When third parties generated or analysed data, this must be clearly stated in Methods and/or Availability sections; corresponding author remains responsible for all data in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions on making third-party data available should be stated; data must be made available for peer review within the terms of data use agreements and ethical/legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of reporting and reporting checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC advocates complete and transparent reporting; for biomedical and biological research, mandatory checklists must be completed before peer review and made available to editors and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strongly recommend using EQUATOR Network minimum reporting guidelines and FAIRsharing.org for reporting checklists. Recommended checklists include CONSORT, SPIRIT, PRISMA/PRISMA-P, STROBE, CARE, COREQ, STARD/TRIPOD, CHEERS, ARRIVE, and discipline-specific statistics checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for systematic review search strategy transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of systematic reviews should provide a link to an additional file reproducing all details of the search strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example presentation guidance referenced (Cochrane Reviewers' Handbook).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods — full reporting and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should include full information on statistical methods and measures used, including justification of appropriateness of tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See SAMPL guidelines. Reviewers will check statistical methods; specialist statistical review may be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource identification and RRIDs
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to include full descriptions of key resources sufficient for unique identification, and are encouraged to use Resource Identifiers (RRIDs) for model organisms, antibodies or tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports the Resource Identification Initiative (RII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell line authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: If human cell lines are used, authors are strongly encouraged to report cell line source (when and where obtained), whether recently authenticated and by what method, and whether recently tested for mycoplasma contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further information from ICLAC; authors recommended to check NCBI database for misidentification/contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized gene nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standardized gene nomenclature throughout (e.g., HGNC for human gene symbols); alternative gene aliases may be reported but not used alone instead of the standard symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists of nomenclature committees and submission routes provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of sequence variants and phenotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Endorse recommendations by Human Variome Project Consortium and HGVS for sequence variants and HPO for phenotypes; submit variants to relevant public gene/disease databases (LSDB) and report database URL and unique identifier in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide identifiers to enable traceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data preparation and community standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to comply with field-specific standards for data preparation/recording and best practices for data sharing, paying attention to patient confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to FAIRsharing for field-specific data standards. For unpublished genomic data, abide by Fort Lauderdale and Toronto guidelines (contact data owners before analyzing unpublished data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital image integrity — accurate representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Final images must accurately represent original data and conform to community standards; authors should exercise caution during data acquisition to avoid misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may request unprocessed data during review or post-publication; retain unprocessed data and metadata ideally in perpetuity. Some journals require submission of unprocessed original images (gels/blots) with final accepted version for Supplementary Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital image general guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not combine images from different times/locations unless clearly indicated; separate adjacent images with borders and label each image in the legend; avoid tools that deliberately alter images (cloning/healing); apply adjustments uniformly across entire figure panels and not selectively emphasize regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to provide original/unprocessed/uncropped images or experimental replicates if originals unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image processing and acquisition tools documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: List all image acquisition tools and software used, including version numbers; fully document acquisition settings and processing steps in Methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If custom code used for processing, provide a full description and make it available in a community repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electrophoretic gels and blots handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Cropping acceptable for clarity if mentioned in figure legend; avoid comparing samples across different gels/blots unless noted; use clear separations (e.g., black lines) when cropping together non-adjacent lanes; include loading controls on same blot where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overexposing gels/blots; if high contrast needed, provide multiple exposures in Supplementary Information. Some journals may require original uncropped images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review and pre-publication history transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Some BMC journals operate open peer review and may publish peer reviewers’ reports, author responses and pre-publication histories associated with articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, reviewer reports will be made available; reviews from closed peer review journals may not be publishable. Reviewers will be asked to make reports available but closed-review reviewers may prefer anonymity; authors transferring from closed to open review contexts may have limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer suggestions and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest potential reviewers and may request exclusion of individuals, but authors should not suggest recent collaborators or colleagues at the same institution and should not exclude too many individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institutional email addresses or identifiers (ORCID/Scopus ID) to help Editors verify identities. Explain reasons for excluded reviewers in the cover letter. Falsifying reviewer information (false name/email) will result in rejection and possible misconduct investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portability of peer review within and between publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC may transfer manuscripts and reviewer reports between BMC journals to reduce re-review; manuscripts may also be considered from other publishers or reviewed by third parties, but transfer does not imply acceptance and receiving journals may require further review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may opt out of sharing; reviewers may indicate they do not wish their report shared with another BMC journal. If transferred to a journal with open peer review, reviewers' reports may be made available where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of manuscripts and reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors treat manuscripts in confidence and reviewers must respect confidentiality and not reveal manuscript details beyond what the journal releases; reviewers should obtain permission before involving colleagues and inform the Editor of any assistants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMC will not share manuscripts outside BMC except in suspected misconduct cases. Participation in BMC research projects will not affect editorial review and manuscript details will be kept confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct policy adherence (COPE)
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC is a COPE member and follows COPE guidelines on handling suspected misconduct; in misconduct cases Editors may share manuscripts with third parties (institutions/ethics committees) and consult Research Integrity Group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of suspected ethical transgression may be included in authors' bibliographic records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If research involving humans/animals wasn't carried out within an appropriate ethical framework the Editor may reject the manuscript and inform institutions or ethics committees; proven misconduct involving published articles may lead to retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer follows COPE guidelines on retraction procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data falsification and fabrication definitions and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Data falsification includes manipulating data to give a false impression (altering images, removing outliers, changing data points); fabrication means making up findings. Editors may request underlying anonymised data and inability to produce original data may lead to rejection or retraction and reporting to institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any integrity concerns during or after peer review referred to Editors who may investigate further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication misconduct and plagiarism detection
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC uses plagiarism detection (CrossCheck); if plagiarism identified, COPE guidelines on plagiarism will be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism detection forms part of routine checks; publication misconduct handled in line with COPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors affecting accuracy but not substantially invalidating conclusions may be corrected via a published Correction linked bidirectionally to the original article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The correction will describe alterations made to the original article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When interpretation or conclusion of an article is substantially undermined it may be necessary to retract; editorial decisions based on reliability and confidence in presented work; Springer follows COPE guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retractions are neutral tools to correct the literature, are indexed and linked; original article watermarked as 'Retracted article:' and title amended accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Expressions of Concern (EEoC) and Editor's Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor's Note alerts readers to initiation of an inquiry and is an online-only update; an Editorial Expression of Concern notifies readers of serious concerns affecting integrity and is published, indexed, given a DOI, and linked; both can be interim measures during investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEoCs are recommended by COPE while investigations are underway and may be superseded by corrections or retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of published content
rubrics_metrics.description: In exceptional circumstances Springer Nature may remove content (article/chapter/book) from online platforms if content is defamatory, infringes rights, unlawful, subject to court/government order, or poses immediate serious health risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal may be temporary or permanent; bibliographic metadata retained with an explanatory statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters Arising (post-publication commentary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal post-publication commentary (challenges, clarifications, replication) may be evaluated, peer-reviewed, and published as Matters Arising; original authors are invited to reply which may be published alongside the commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should reflect knowledge available at time of original paper, not later developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals against rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may appeal a rejection by contacting the Editor; appeals are secondary to normal workload and may take weeks. Only one appeal is permitted per manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals considered generally only if: (a) an error in the review/editorial process determined the decision, (b) important additional data can be provided, or (c) a convincing case of bias is demonstrated. Appeals should include manuscript tracking number and may require an appeal form; successful appeals may lead to further peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints about processes handled initially by the Editor responsible; complaints about publication ethics/scientific content follow COPE guidelines and may be escalated to Springer Nature Research Integrity Group; unresolved complaints can be escalated to editorial/publishing management or ethics.reporting@springernature.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complaints about the Editor, contact the editorial and publishing management team via the provided email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections and Special Issues review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to BMC Journal Collections or Special Issues are assessed by the journal’s standard editorial criteria and are subject to all standard editorial policies (e.g., competing interests); content is also checked for fit to the Collection/Special Issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review follows the journal’s standard process. If editors of the Collection/Special Issue have competing interests, another Editor without competing interests will handle their evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act with integrity expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers, staff and stakeholders are expected to uphold honesty, accountability, fairness and compliance with legal and ethical standards; breaches may lead to withdrawal of manuscripts or post-publication actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature may bring serious cases to employers or authorities and refuse interactions with repeat offenders. Investigations after publication may lead to corrective actions.
